name: Maguro
alt: A reddish-pink slice of raw fish draped over a small mound of rice.
facts: This deep red fish is one of the most popular sushi fish in the whole world.
It can swim in fast bursts, which is part of why it's prized for its firm, meaty texture.

name: Sake
alt: A bright orange-pink slice of raw fish on top of a small mound of rice.
facts: This is the single most popular fish used in sushi in the United States.
Its bright orange color comes partly from the tiny shrimp-like creatures it eats in the wild.

name: Hamachi
alt: A pale, glossy slice of raw white fish over a mound of rice.
facts: This fish is named for a yellow stripe that runs along its side.
Chefs prize it for a buttery, mild flavor that's milder than redder sushi fish.

name: Ebi
alt: A curled, pink-and-white cooked shellfish draped over a mound of rice.
facts: This topping is cooked first, then split open and laid flat over the rice.
Its curled shape and pink-and-white stripes make it easy to spot on a sushi plate.

name: Unagi
alt: A glossy, dark-brown grilled topping glazed with sauce, laid over rice.
facts: This topping is grilled and brushed with a sweet, sticky sauce before serving.
Unlike most sushi toppings, it's never served raw.

name: Tako
alt: A pale, bumpy-textured slice with a reddish-purple edge draped over rice.
facts: This topping is boiled until tender, which turns its edge from gray to a reddish-purple.
Its bumpy texture comes from rows of tiny suckers.

name: Ika
alt: A smooth, milky-white slice with fine crisscross markings over a mound of rice.
facts: Chefs score this topping with tiny crisscross cuts so it's easier to chew.
It has a mild flavor and a slightly chewy, springy texture.

name: Hotate
alt: A round, pale ivory-colored piece of shellfish resting on a mound of rice.
facts: This topping comes from a shellfish that can actually swim by clapping its shell open and shut.
It has a naturally sweet taste and a soft, tender bite.

name: Ikura
alt: A small cup of rice wrapped in seaweed and piled high with glistening orange eggs.
facts: This topping is made of hundreds of tiny, glistening orange eggs.
Each little egg pops gently when you bite into it.

name: Uni
alt: A soft, golden-yellow, custard-like topping piled in a small seaweed-wrapped cup of rice.
facts: This topping comes from a spiky sea creature and has a soft, custardy texture.
Its color can range from pale yellow to deep orange depending on where it's harvested.

name: Toro
alt: A pale pink slice of fish with light marbled streaks draped over rice.
facts: This topping comes from the fattiest part of the fish, which makes it melt in your mouth.
Its pale, marbled streaks look a little like a slice of fine steak.

name: Anago
alt: A pale, soft, light-brown topping laid flat over a mound of rice.
facts: This topping is simmered until tender instead of being grilled.
It's a lighter, milder cousin of another popular grilled eel topping.

name: Tamago
alt: A few thick, golden-yellow slices of a sweet, layered omelette stacked on a plate.
facts: This topping is made from a lightly sweetened omelette, cooked in thin layers and rolled up.
It's one of the few sushi toppings that's a favorite with kids who don't love seafood.

name: Saba
alt: Pieces of fish with shiny, dark striped skin on top and pale flesh below, resting on rice.
facts: This topping is cured in salt and vinegar before serving, which gives it a tangy bite.
Its skin is left on and has a shiny, striped pattern.

name: Amaebi
alt: A pale pink, glossy raw shellfish draped over a mound of rice.
facts: This shellfish is served raw, with a soft texture and a delicate, sweet flavor.
Chefs sometimes fry the head separately afterward as a crunchy little snack.

name: California Roll
alt: A sushi roll with rice on the outside, dotted with small orange roe, and a creamy filling visible inside.
facts: This roll was invented in North America, not Japan, as an easier introduction to sushi.
It's usually rolled with the seaweed on the inside and rice on the outside, so it looks less unusual to new sushi eaters.
It typically combines creamy avocado, crab, and cucumber.

name: Spicy Tuna Roll
alt: A sushi roll with a reddish, fiery-looking filling, held up with chopsticks.
facts: This roll mixes chopped raw fish with a fiery, creamy sauce before rolling it up.
It's one of the most popular rolls ordered at sushi restaurants in the U.S.

name: Dragon Roll
alt: A sushi roll topped with overlapping thin green slices arranged like scales.
facts: Thin slices of avocado are arranged on top to look like a mythical creature's scaly skin.
It's often filled with fried shrimp and cucumber.

name: Rainbow Roll
alt: A sushi roll topped with many different colored raw fish slices laid side by side.
facts: Several different colorful raw fish are draped over the top, one slice of each, in a row.
Underneath the colorful topping is usually a roll a lot like the very first popular American sushi roll.

name: Philadelphia Roll
alt: A sushi roll with a creamy white filling and a pink fish topping draped over rice.
facts: This roll combines smoked salmon with a soft, tangy cream cheese filling.
It mixes a Japanese cooking tradition with an ingredient more typically found on a bagel.

name: Spider Roll
alt: A sushi roll with crispy fried legs sticking out from both ends.
facts: This roll is filled with a whole deep-fried soft-shell crab, legs and all.
The crab's crispy legs often stick out from the ends of the roll.

name: Caterpillar Roll
alt: A sushi roll topped with overlapping thin green avocado slices that look like a small creature's segmented back.
facts: Thin slices of avocado are layered on top to resemble a small creature's segmented body.
It's usually filled with grilled eel and cucumber.

name: Alaska Roll
alt: A sushi roll with a pink fish topping over a pale green and white filling.
facts: This roll combines raw salmon with creamy avocado and crisp cucumber.
It's named for the cold northern Pacific waters its main ingredient often comes from.

name: Negitoro Roll
alt: A sushi cup wrapped in seaweed and filled with finely chopped, marbled pink fish flecked with green onion.
facts: This roll is filled with finely chopped fatty tuna mixed with chopped green onion.
Because the fish is scraped and minced rather than sliced, it has a soft, almost creamy texture.

name: Futomaki
alt: A thick, large sushi roll cut into rounds, with several different colorful fillings visible inside.
facts: This roll is rolled extra thick, often with five or more different fillings packed inside.
It often includes cooked ingredients like egg and simmered vegetables, not just raw fish.

name: Tekka Maki
alt: A small sushi roll cut into rounds, filled with a single strip of dark red fish in the center.
facts: This roll is one of the simplest on a sushi menu: just one ingredient rolled up with rice and seaweed.
Its name is said to come from gambling parlors, where it was a quick snack players could eat without getting their cards greasy.

name: Kappa Maki
alt: A small sushi roll cut into rounds, with a pale green vegetable strip visible in the center.
facts: This roll contains no fish at all -- just a crunchy vegetable filling.
It's named after a mischievous water spirit from Japanese folklore that's said to love this vegetable.

name: Unagi Roll
alt: A sushi roll topped with glossy, dark-glazed grilled strips.
facts: This roll is filled with a sweet, grilled topping that's brushed with a sticky glaze.
Its filling is always cooked, never served raw.

name: Volcano Roll
alt: A sushi roll piled high with a warm, mounded, creamy orange topping.
facts: This roll is topped with a warm, baked, creamy mixture that's sometimes briefly torched before serving.
Its bumpy, mounded topping is meant to look like a small eruption.

name: Shrimp Tempura Roll
alt: A sushi roll with a golden, crispy fried tail peeking out from one end.
facts: This roll is filled with a shellfish that's been battered and deep-fried until crunchy.
Because the shellfish is fried whole, it gives the roll a crispy bite in the middle instead of a chewy one.
